note: Discovery leads for topic workers. Every topic must still research and verify its own sources; nothing here is pre-approved for reuse. Date every statistic. Prefer government and intergovernmental primary sources for definitions, economic data, and food-safety rules; treat industry-association and proprietary-benchmark material as REFERENCE_ONLY.

tierA.provider: Bureau of Labor Statistics Occupational Outlook Handbook
tierA.useFor: hospitality/tourism roles, wages, employment, outlook — date figures (lodging managers, chefs, meeting/event planners, food service managers)
the model retail food-safety code: temperatures, HACCP principles, employee health — note it is a MODEL code adopted variably by states/localities

tierA.provider: BEA Travel and Tourism Satellite Accounts (TTSA)
tierA.useFor: tourism's measured contribution to U.S. GDP and employment — date every figure

tierA.provider: National Travel and Tourism Office (ITA, U.S. Dept. of Commerce)
tierA.useFor: U.S. inbound/outbound travel data and definitions
international definitions of tourism/visitor/tourist, global arrivals data, sustainable-tourism definition — date figures

tierB.provider: OpenStax / Open Textbook Library — hospitality & tourism OER
tierB.useFor: open hospitality/tourism management texts (e.g., 'Introduction to Tourism and Hospitality in BC', 'Introduction to Hospitality')
sustainable-tourism criteria — describe the framework, do not reproduce the criteria text
U.S. lodging industry structure and data — REFERENCE_ONLY, verify underlying figures and date them
U.S. travel economic-impact data — secondary; verify and date
global travel & tourism economic impact — secondary; verify and date
food-handler training concepts — COPYRIGHTED, REFERENCE_ONLY; describe, never reproduce

cautions: This is a consumer-facing, applied subject. Teach concepts and industry practice; give no individualized business, legal, franchise, tax, investment, or employment-law advice.

Food safety must be accurate and taught from the FDA Food Code, CDC, and FoodSafety.gov. State that the Food Code is a MODEL code adopted and enforced variably by state and local jurisdictions, and that this is educational content, not a substitute for a certified food-handler/manager course or local health-code compliance. ServSafe and other proprietary curricula are copyrighted — REFERENCE_ONLY, never reproduce their materials.

Revenue-management and lodging metrics (occupancy, ADR, RevPAR) should be taught with their formulas and worked with real arithmetic executed in Bash. STR/CoStar and other proprietary benchmark data are REFERENCE_ONLY — do not reproduce their datasets; use hypothetical or clearly public figures for examples.

Tourism statistics are time-sensitive and come in incompatible measures. Date every figure and name the source; distinguish UN Tourism's international definitions and global arrivals from U.S. domestic measures (BEA Travel and Tourism Satellite Accounts for GDP/employment contribution; the National Travel and Tourism Office for inbound/outbound). Do not sum across incompatible series.

Attribute service-quality and management frameworks to their originators (e.g., SERVQUAL to Parasuraman, Zeithaml & Berry; the service-recovery paradox as a studied and debated effect, not a guaranteed outcome). Represent contested ideas (overtourism, carrying capacity, the recovery paradox) as discussed and attributed, not settled.

Sustainable tourism: use UN Tourism's definition and the GSTC criteria framework; attribute them. Present sustainability trade-offs and overtourism as genuine debates; avoid marketing/greenwashing language.

Wage, tipping, and employment rules vary by jurisdiction (federal vs state tipped-minimum-wage, for example). State figures with their year and source and note the variation; give no legal or payroll advice.
Distribute question answer keys evenly across positions A/B/C/D and use position A at least once per topic; prior subjects skewed the correct answer away from position D.
